title: Changing demonstrative statements into negatives
summary: Replace on or ovat with the matching negative olla construction.
objectives: Read the affirmative source and negative target meanings.
Replace ovat with eivät ole while preserving the subject.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: A controlled transformation changes only the polarity of the supplied statement.
Singular on becomes ei ole; plural ovat becomes eivät ole.

sections.title: Use one clear decision
paragraphs: Keep the demonstrative, noun, and context unchanged.
Both source and target meanings remain visible before the learner responds.

examples.english: The previously identified house is not here.
steps: Se talo: the complete singular subject is supplied.
ole: fixed form after the negative verb.

examples.english: These books are not at home.
steps: Nämä kirjat: the complete plural subject is supplied.
ole: fixed form after the negative verb.

examples.english: That book is not at home.
steps: Tuo kirja: the complete singular subject is supplied.
ole: fixed form after the negative verb.

commonMistakes: Do not change the demonstrative during the transformation.
Do not use a plural negative form for a singular source.
Do not retain on or ovat after the negative verb.

“eivät” is the plural negative verb; use “ei”, the singular negative verb.
“on” is the singular affirmative form of olla; use “ei”, the singular negative verb.
